correctness.rationale: Free amalgamation across the named base cannot create a tournament spanning the two sides. Homogeneity and the finite extension property therefore give one nonalgebraic type per admissible arc pattern. On an occupied old edge both new arcs are forced to close a directed triangle, so each selected nonsingleton path has one compatible labeling unless it contains a through-centered triple. The fully selected cycle has exactly one labeling only in the defect-free case. A defect set is realizable exactly in the stated parity, with two sign assignments each. Containment of defect sets orders the polynomials; odd-cycle singleton defect sets are rotations. The n consecutive triples are distinct even at n=4, and the single-edge and independent triple counts are n(n-4) and n(n-4)(n-5)/6. This proves strictness against the corresponding extremum at degree three. The transfer trace counts each indexed word with the correct power of z; at z=1 its primitive minimum and positive two-edge maximum transfers have the stated characteristic polynomials. The odd trace has a positive Perron amplitude because the remaining one-edge factor has positive pairing with the Perron vectors. A fresh finite check constructs each candidate ternary pattern's tournament outdegrees directly: all 240 orientations of orders 4–7 agree with the support formula and extremal counts. This is corroboration, not an all-order proof.

value.rationale: An induced cycle is the first natural closed extension base beyond a path. The result quantifies how the directions of named old arcs limit extension freedom, locates the first orientation-sensitive coefficient, and proves a common extremum for every degree, not merely for the total. The unavoidable odd defect and exponential separation of the two total counts give structural content beyond an isolated finite enumeration.
